title: Can’t believe 6 years later I finally saw this show again!  #SingStre...
transcript: One of my musical theater Roman Empires is the Broadway musical Sing Street, which was supposed to come to Broadway in March 2020 after a successful off Broadway run, but then the pandemic happened and it never came. I even have a poster from the canceled Broadway run on my wall. Now the show is getting another chance in London's West End, and obviously I had to go see it. It is pretty much the same production that played off Broadway six years ago. It is the same creative team, the general design is the same. However, it is a whole new cast, and they've made several revisions to the material. Most notable are three new songs, including a brand new opening, which I think is fantastic. The other two are solos for Rafina and the older brother character. And while I didn't think either of them were super necessary additions, it was nice to see these characters get moments to shine that they didn't have in the original production. But other than that, it's mostly small changes like moving things around. The projection design got a massive glow up. It is stunning. But at its core, the heart of the show is still the same. It is still about a bunch of Irish kids using music as a means to find themselves, to find their voice. And it is those themes of music as expression, music as rebellion that keep me coming back to this piece. Why I really hope that It has another life beyond this production, whether that is transferring to another West End theater or coming back to New York. Because while the show is not without its flaws, I do think this is the best the show has ever been.
